clue.text: Soft tissue on me thrown over into grave

indicators.note: into says the jumbled letters go inside the grave word

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound, a grave

indicators.note: thrown over suggests the two little words are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Soft flesh is tipped over into a grave, a grisly burial scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown over' jumbles ON ME to ONEM, which goes 'into' BARROW after its B. A barrow here is the burial mound, not a wheelbarrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone marrow is the soft fatty tissue filling the cavities inside bones.

clue.text: Secure standard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fasten with a bent wire clip
second meaning: a basic, regular item

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a phrase about safety, but each is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means fasten with wire clips; as a noun it is a basic, routinely used commodity.

clue.text: Capital city in trouble is on the up after support of women

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment for women

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, the opposite way

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A capital city is in trouble but on the way up after support from women voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia has been the purpose-built capital of Brazil since 1960.

clue.text: One of seven papers in conflict

indicators.note: the papers are placed in the word for conflict, sitting inside it

parts.note: a fray is a fight or conflict
ID is identification, one's papers

explanation.surface: One of seven newspapers caught up in a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers, but here it means identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday is one of the seven days of the week, so 'one of seven' is a fair cryptic definition.

clue.text: Last seen in canteen I guess, tool brought up for refuse collector

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, reversing it
the last thing seen in a word is its final letter, so only the end of canteen is kept

parts.note: the final letter of canteen
taken as written
to bet is to guess at an outcome
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone in a canteen guesses at a tool before taking out the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces are joined and then the whole string is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste bin collects refuse, so 'refuse collector' is a playful description rather than a dustman.

clue.text: Sound of stringed instrument, one telling a story

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is pronounced, so we want a word spoken the same way

parts.note: a lyre is an ancient harp-like instrument

explanation.surface: A musician tells a tale to the sound of a harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling a story' is the idiom for lying, not narrating.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a story is an idiom for telling a lie, so the person doing it is a fibber.

clue.text: Bird, one poking around gobbling crumbs ultimately

indicators.note: to gobble something is to swallow it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: a rooter is one who roots about, poking around

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of crumbs is used

parts.note: the last letter of crumbs

explanation.surface: A bird pecking about and gobbling up crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Where twelve numbers may appear, always

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally around a clock face, which carries twelve numerals
second meaning: all day and night, continuously

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic, literal reading of a clock face; the second is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for continuously, day and night, and literally describes the ring of hours on a dial.

clue.text: Study of literature in English university

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the University of ..., in Berkshire

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town west of London with its own university.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is the act of perusing books, and it is also the name of a town with a university in southern England.

clue.text: Neighbourly type from somewhere in India installing radio mast for broadcasting

indicators.note: installing means putting inside, so the Goa word goes round the rest

parts.note: Goan means from Goa, a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters of the two words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from an Indian state puts up a radio mast for transmissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For broadcasting' jumbles RADIO MAST to ODSAMARIT, which GOAN is 'installing' after its GO. The radio talk invites a transmitting sense, but broadcasting here scatters letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Good Samaritan, from the parable in Luke's gospel, is anyone who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Closet open, used mysteriously to hide cross

definitions.note: used as an adjective, closet means secret, kept hidden

indicators.note: to hide means to keep something inside, so the jumbled letters go round the cross
mysteriously suggests the letters behave in a puzzling way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A cupboard is open, used in some mysterious way to conceal a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mysteriously' jumbles OPEN USED to UNEPOSED, and 'to hide' puts X inside it after UNE. 'Closet' looks like a cupboard noun but is the adjective meaning secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet habit is kept secret, so it has not been revealed to anyone.

clue.text: Trunk roughly attached to elephant at last

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of elephant
'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk, described as roughly attached at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' tempts toward the elephant, but it is the human body without head or limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, the part left without head, arms and legs.

clue.text: Male billed as an old sailor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a male creature with a bill, a male duck
second meaning: Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan navigator

explanation.walkthrough: 'Billed as' reads like advertising, but 'billed' means having a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the male of the duck and the famous Elizabethan seafarer who circumnavigated the globe.

clue.text: In the outskirts of Leeds, there's always a fight for good-for-nothings

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed in between the outer letters, sitting inside them
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Leeds
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
taken as written
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: On the edge of Leeds, idlers are always up for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: AY meaning always is an old poetic word, still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Layabouts are lazy idlers who avoid work, the same as good-for-nothings.

clue.text: Where are the clouds? Not sure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally aloft in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered literally by the phrase, which is also the idiom for unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for undecided or unresolved, and literally describes clouds overhead in the sky.

clue.text: Spicy sauce, mostly strong is it?

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: hard means strong, as in a hard drink
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A question whether a spicy sauce is, for the most part, a strong one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims HARD to HAR. 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention from the 1920s phrase for allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste used to season dishes such as couscous.

clue.text: Serious passage read out

indicators.note: reading something out loud means the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a strait is a narrow sea passage

explanation.surface: Someone gives a solemn reading of a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a piece of text, but here it is a narrow channel of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a straight face means remaining serious, and a straight answer is earnest.

clue.text: Establish name in two companies

indicators.note: the name sits in between the two companies, enclosed by them

parts.note: first company: CO, the abbreviation for company
N is short for name

explanation.surface: A business arrangement sets up a name across two companies.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish its truth or validity, as when a test confirms a fact.

clue.text: Wood, funny old thing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the timber of the ... tree
second meaning: a stale, overused joke

explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny old thing' sounds like an affectionate remark, but it is a joke that is old.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is a hardwood timber, and an old chestnut is a joke told so often it has grown stale.

clue.text: Fear those spotted behind bovine are dropping back

indicators.note: behind says the spotted things come after the bovine word and its partner

parts.note: a cow is a bovine animal

indicators.note: dropping back means the last letter of the word falls away

parts.note: dice are spotted with dots on each face

explanation.surface: Animals with spots trail behind a cow and fall back in alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping back' leaves AR from ARE; 'those spotted' are dice, the cubes marked with spots, placed 'behind' COW AR. 'Spotted' first suggests seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is a lack of courage, a giving way to fear.

clue.text: I feast beneath the moon

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed beneath another is written after it, so the feast comes second

parts.note: Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
to dine is to feast

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a moonlit dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the chemical symbol. In a down clue, 'beneath' puts the feast below the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol for the element iodine.

clue.text: Unpleasant type rat, he is horrible

indicators.note: something horrible is in a terrible state, so its letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of work denounced as a horrible rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is a person full of hostility towards others, which makes for an unpleasant character.

clue.text: Fragrant hugs beginning to excite as a result

indicators.note: to hug is to hold within one's arms, so one word enfolds the other

parts.note: herby means smelling of herbs, fragrant

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of excite

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling partner's embrace starts to arouse, with some consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereby is a formal adverb meaning by this means or as a result of this.

clue.text: Arabian person in attention-seeker?

indicators.note: the person is placed in the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: 'Oi!' is a shout to get someone's attention
a man is a person

explanation.surface: Is a person from Arabia just craving attention?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention-seeker' looks like a show-off, but it is the call 'Oi!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani comes from Oman, a country on the Arabian Peninsula, so the word is an Arabian adjective.

clue.text: Book already commencing, the story starts

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A book whose story starts straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commencing' reads as part of the surface but is one of the four source words; 'starts' alone signals taking first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts, the Acts of the Apostles, is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Check fellow is cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to check or hold back
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: An inspector checks whether the man is the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person, but it is a cleaning substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, the substance used to wash dishes and clothes.

clue.text: Thicken stews — here?

indicators.note: to stew is to cook ingredients together until they break down, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of the word

explanation.surface: Asking where one thickens a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the wordplay, and it also asks where thickening and stewing happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is the room where food is cooked, so it is where sauces are thickened and stews made.

clue.text: I'm not sure boy is Italian

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation
Brian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over whether a boy is Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Umbria is a region of central Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Umbrian comes from Umbria, a region of central Italy, so is an Italian.
